headlines.summary: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms
headlines.article_text: Tesla, SpaceX stocks fall after 2026 midterms Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap in the two days after midterms. As Democrats control the House and Senate, and Texas flips blue, investors expect Musk and his companies to face probes and steeper regulatory hurdles to their AI and merger ambitions. Musk was the biggest backer of GOP candidates and causes in the midterms and most of those he backed were defeated by Dem opponents. In this article TSLA SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT SpaceX CEO Elon Musk looks on as President Donald Trump speaks to the press after a meeting with technology executives about artificial intelligence at the White House in Washington, Sept. 29, 2026. Kent Nishimura | AFP | Getty Images SpaceX and Tesla shares declined by about 9% and 11%, respectively, on Thursday afternoon with investors concerned that Elon Musk could face new congressional probes, and his companies could face stricter regulation following U.S. midterm elections. The declines, which correlated with a broader tech selloff , brought aggregate market cap losses for SpaceX and Tesla to over $420 billion since Tuesday's close. Musk's wealth, which had topped $1 trillion after SpaceX's IPO in June, is now down below $800 billion, having dropped about $90 billion in the past week, according to Forbes . He is still the richest man in the world. Musk was the biggest donor to GOP candidates and causes in the midterms, with his financial contributions exceeding $470 million , the FT first reported. Despite his bolstering the GOP war chest, most of the candidates Musk backed lost their races . Democrats won control of both the House and Senate. And in Texas, where both Tesla and SpaceX are headquartered, Democrats Sen.-elect James Talarico and Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa beat long-time Musk allies, Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott. Deutsche Bank analysts wrote in a note out on Wednesday, "While policy is naturally hard to predict, we could envision SpaceX facing some incremental headwinds in this type of backdrop." Texas' Gov. elect Hinojosa "made data centers a major campaign issue," the analysts noted, calling for "a moratorium on new approvals until the legislature passes stronger protections on water use, electricity costs, local control, and incentives," and criticizing tax breaks for large facilities. Tesla and SpaceX are both building out AI infrastructure in Texas, and are planning to build Terafab, a massive facility, which will include a data center and sprawling semiconductor factory, in Grimes County, Texas. SpaceX also plans to build out a "supercomputer" at its Starbase, Texas launch facility and company town, according to company job listings . Deutsche Bank analysts also wrote that SpaceX's Texas compute capacity could now be at risk of delays. Capital expenditures by the company may need to increase to meet the requirements of tighter, anticipated regulations around data center buildout, the analysts wrote. Musk and SpaceX have been instructed to preserve records concerning restrictions they imposed on a military version of their Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, CNN first reported , citing an aide to a Democratic Senator. The restrictions hampered the country's ability to defend against attacks by Russia. Additionally, regulatory scrutiny could block chances for Musk to merge SpaceX and Tesla, an idea he has promoted, while acknowledging shareholders' approval would be required first. SpaceX and Tesla had lost about $456 billion in market cap by the close of business on Thursday. In this article IREN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Thomas Fuller | SOPA Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Following a 26% post-election plunge in its stock price, neocloud IREN said in its earnings report on Thursday that over $4 billion in annual recurring revenue projected to land in 2026 has been pushed out to at least January. IREN said the move, which could extend payment to February, is due to "a customer-requested change and supplier timing." Shares of IREN rose in extended trading, but that comes after a 55% drop over the past month. The company said revenue climbed 66% from the prior quarter to $228 million, beating the $221 million average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. AI Cloud revenue more than doubled to $200 million. IREN gets the rest of its revenue from bitcoin mining, which was its primary business before the company pivoted to AI. IREN's net loss narrowed to $263 million from $684 million from the prior period. Year-ago figures weren't included in the earnings release. The company is being closely watched by investors as the AI trade shows signs of unwinding , particularly following the Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterm elections. Concerns are mounting that cash-burning companies reliant on debt are going to have a hard time meeting their obligations as interest rates rise and lenders back out of the market. The Nasdaq had its worst day on Thursday since April 2025. CoreWeave , which is set to report earnings on Tuesday, has plunged 60% in the past month. Nebius , which reports next Thursday, is down 48% over that stretch. IREN said revenue backlog increased 22% from the prior period to $20.3 billion, with "approximately two-thirds with investment-grade counterparties." The $4 billion ARR target is fully contracted and funded, the company said. "There is a disconnect between what we're seeing in public market and what we're seeing at the customer level," IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts told CNBC's Seema Mody. Still, Iren said it planed to shell out $15 billion in capital expenditures the rest of this fiscal year, including $9 billion in cash and committed financing, and $6 billion in "target" financing, which is "subject to market conditions." The neocloud said that prices for its compute continues to rise and that it expanded an existing contract with a leading frontier AI lab. headlines.title: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: DraftKings, Cloudflare, Airbnb, Atlassian & more
headlines.summary: Here are the companies making headlines in extended trading.
headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: DKNG, NET, ABNB, TEAM Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are the companies making headlines in extended trading. Airbnb — The vacation rental platform jumped 11%. Airbnb reported third-quarter earnings of $3.16 per share, topping analysts' consensus estimate of $2.85, while revenue of $4.87 billion beat the Street's $4.75 billion, LSEG data showed. Atlassian — The supplier of team collaboration and productivity software dropped more than 15%. Atlassian's latest financials showed year-over-year data center revenue growth expected to decline approximately 14% in the fiscal second quarter ending in December, and 16% in the fiscal year ending next June. Affirm Holdings — Shares of the buy now, pay later company tumbled 11% after projections for second-quarter revenue only narrowly topped estimates. Affirm sees revenue ranging from $1.435 billion to $1.465 billion, while the LSEG consensus estimate called for $1.43 billion. Wynn Resorts — The casino operator fell 1% after third-quarter results missed Wall Street's expectations. Wynn earned 33 cents a share on an adjusted basis and revenue came in at $1.69 billion. Analysts were looking for 68 cents a share and $1.75 billion, per LSEG. Akamai Technologies — Shares of the cloud computing company dropped 1% following disappointing projections for the fourth quarter. Akamai sees adjusted earnings in a range of $1.50 to $1.70 per share on revenue of $1.145 billion to $1.17 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $1.78 per share and $1.20 billion. Cloudflare — The cloud company surged 14% after guidance for the current quarter topped the Street's expectations. Cloudflare anticipates adjusted earnings of 43 cents a share on revenue ranging from $845 million to $846 million. Analysts polled by LSEG sought 38 cents a share and $798 million. Third-quarter results also beat analysts' estimates. JFrog — The software company popped 25% after raising its full-year guidance. JFrog sees adjusted earnings ranging from $1.14 to $1.16 per share on revenue of $680 million to $682 million. The outlook trounced the FactSet consensus estimate for 98 cents a share and $651.9 million. DraftKings — The online sports betting platform tanked 22% after the company posted a wider-than-expected third-quarter loss. DraftKings posted a loss of 94 cents per share, worse than the 39 cents per share loss analysts polled by LSEG anticipated. Revenue of $1.33 billion fell short of the $1.40 billion estimate. Sportsbook revenue for the period came in at $784 million, missing the $811.8 million StreetAccount consensus estimate. Axon Enterprise — The maker of Taser electric weapons slid 13% postmarket after dropping almost 10% during regular trading Thursday. Third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.72 was short of analysts' consensus of $1.89, while revenue of $909 million also missed the Street's $934.3 million, according to FactSet data. Lyft — The ridesharing company fell more than 5%. Fourth-quarter guidance for bookings came in at $5.74 billion to $5.94 billion, versus the FactSet consensus of $5.81 billion. CNBC's Scott Schnipper contributed reporting.

headlines.title: Nasdaq drops into correction territory — here’s what typically happens next
headlines.summary: Nasdaq’s slide into correction territory puts its history of recoveries in focus. Here's what history shows.
headlines.article_text: Nasdaq drops into correction territory — here’s what typically happens next Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article .IXIC NDAQ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The Nasdaq building is pictured on April 20, 2026 in New York City. Zamek | View Press | Corbis News | Getty Images The Nasdaq Composite plunged into correction territory on Thursday. History shows more selling can follow in the near term, but a recovery eventually takes hold three months later. The tech-heavy index slid more than 5% on Thursday, closing more than 11% below its record reached last month. On Wall Street, any decline greater than 10% is a correction. A 20% pullback qualifies as a bear market. Across 10 previous correction episodes over the last decade, selloffs in 2025, 2022, 2020 and 2018 were followed by further rough selling over the next one month. But the Nasdaq was back to rally mode again after six months for all those occasions except one: 2022. Overall, the Nasdaq gained an average of 9.41% from the correction bottom over the following three months and 17.03% over six months. The January 2022 correction was the one that offered a harsher outcome. The Nasdaq lost another 18.3% over the next six months and was down 24.3% a year later. Nasdaq Composite Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells The catalyst for this correction was Democrats sweeping the House and Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections. The party also made significant gains in Texas, where Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor after campaigning on an immediate moratorium for data center development. Investors are now weighing whether tighter state-level restrictions could slow data center construction, putting pressure on companies tied to the artificial intelligence trade. Frank Cappelleri, founder of CappThesis, pointed to past midterm election cycles for guidance and found that points to more volatility in the near term as well. The chart analyst said the Nasdaq was higher 12 months after the election in all but one of 13 midterm cycles since 1974. "The caveat is that the path can be a volatile one," he said. Cappelleri pointed to 2018, when the Nasdaq rallied the day after Democrats won the House. A sharp December sell-off followed, but the index was ultimately about 15% higher a year after the election, he said. Chip stocks tumbled Thursday, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) falling 12% and for its worst day since the Covid-19 breakout of March 2020. — CNBC's Fred Imbert contributed to the report Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.
